And they persisted in this attitude until the end, so that even if it happened that Israel shared in misfortunes brought upon itself by God, they rejoiced and gloated over them, those who accused God of being utterly unable to do anything, the God who promised to save those who worship him. And the blessed Jeremiah is a witness of this in his vision against them, saying: 'The horn of Moab is broken, and its strength is shattered. Make him drunk, for he has exalted himself against the Lord.' And again: 'Thus the Lord has said: Arioth is taken, and the fortresses are seized. And Moab shall perish from among the people, because he has exalted himself against the Lord.' For indeed at intervals the tyrant of 70,400 Assyrians and Babylonians came, devastating Judah. He captured the cities of Samaria. But the Moabites, again mocking the destroyed, celebrated immoderately and reproached, they were scattering the glory of God. Thus they too are given over to desolation, utterly destroyed together with cities and people and every house, so that now it seems they may not even exist. Therefore the vision mentioned before remembers these things that have happened to them: clearly from above wrath, and it says: 'At night the Moabite perishes.'

pass_b_english: And Israel was inaccessible, and thus they were exceedingly bitter and malicious in disposition, withdrawing their support and persuading others to attack against the God over all.

This attitude persisted until the end, and even when Israel suffered misfortunes brought upon itself by God, they rejoiced and gloated over them, those who accused God of being utterly unable to do anything, the God who promised to save those who worship him.
The prophet Jeremiah bears witness to this in his vision against them, declaring that their strength is shattered and they will be made drunk for exalting themselves against the Lord.
Jeremiah says, 'The horn of Moab is broken, and its strength is shattered. Make him drunk, for he has exalted himself against the Lord.' (Jeremiah 48:2-3)
Furthermore, Jeremiah says that Arioth is taken and the fortresses are seized, and Moab will perish from among the people because they have exalted themselves against the Lord. (Jeremiah 48:24)
For indeed at intervals the tyrant of 70,400 Assyrians and Babylonians came, devastating Judah and capturing the cities of Samaria.
Meanwhile, the Moabites, mocking the destroyed nation, celebrated immoderately and reproached, while they were scattering the glory of God.
Thus they too are given over to desolation, utterly destroyed together with their cities, people, and every house, to the point where it seems they may not even exist.
The vision mentioned earlier remembers these events that have happened to them, clearly demonstrating wrath from above, and says, 'At night the Moabite perishes.' (Jeremiah 48:20)
For the wall of the Moabite territory was destroyed by night.

According to some investigators, when the Babylonians were about to wage war against the Moabites, an earthquake occurred, devastating the metropolis and causing its wall to collapse by itself in the night and darkness, before the enemies even approached, and the Moabites' hope of salvation perished.

The Moabites had become terrible and uncultured, and having emboldened themselves by the deceits of demons, and by means of magical art seeking to increase themselves against the whole hand, and even of Israel itself, if God should defend it.
Therefore, in the so-called Lebedon, their altar was and a sanctuary not insignificant, which place they had come to build.
There they performed divinations, thought greatly, and held the place most sacred above all others.
But it is said that Lebedon, where the Moabites' altar is, will be destroyed, and the workshop of their divination will be destroyed.

The prophet warns the Moabites, saying, 'But lament, for yourselves'; for they had often raised their eyebrows high, delighting in the misfortunes of others, but now the war runs against them themselves, and the damage from here onward hangs upon the heads of their impieties. (Jeremiah 48:31)
The Moabites are told to lament for themselves, for they had often raised their eyebrows high, delighting in the misfortunes of others.
